blocks.text: A place where human history and nature meet, the Mediterranean Basin is located in a unique geographical position, with unparalleled environmental heterogeneity and a biodiversity that is nothing short of extraordinary. It is no coincidence that it is identified as one of the 25 biodiversity hotspots globally, but its warming also classifies it as a climate change hotspot. From the urban to the marine ecosystem, there is no ecosystem that is not affected by the effects of climate change. In the future of the cradle of human civilization, an increase in drought and the formation of arid lands is therefore expected. The Mediterranean Basin risks being swallowed up by the vortex of the new era of the Anthropocene. The situation is amplified by the fact that it is a fundamentally closed area, by the intensive use of its soil, by the urbanization and pollution of the regions that overlook this sea.
